title: CBC Recommends Voting Yes on November Ballot Questions 2, 3, 4, and 5 to Boost Housing Production in New York
plain_title: Group backs four ballot questions on land use and housing
what_they_audited: A Citizens Budget Commission report on four November ballot questions proposed by the New York City Charter Revision Commission (CRC) dealing with land use review and the City Map.
background: Three of the questions would change the city's land use decision-making process and one would change how the City Map is administered.

findings.plain: The city has a severe shortage of housing, pushing up rents and home prices.
findings.quote: New York City has a dire housing shortage, burdening too many New Yorkers with ever-higher rents and home prices.

findings.plain: Private rezoning applications take years to get through the current review process.
findings.quote: Too long, with private rezoning application approval taking between 2 to 3 years

findings.plain: The group's research puts the added cost of the land use process at tens of thousands of dollars per apartment.
findings.quote: Too expensive, adding as much as $82,000 to the cost of each housing unit in 2025 dollars

findings.plain: The proposed Affordable Housing Fast Track would apply in the community districts that permitted the least affordable housing over the previous five years.
findings.quote: The Affordable Housing Fast Track would speed up production in the 12 Community Districts that permitted the least affordable housing over the preceding five years.

findings.plain: Question 4 would let a three-member board overturn a City Council disapproval or modification of certain affordable housing projects.
findings.quote: A board consisting of the Mayor, City Council Speaker, and Borough President would be able to overturn a Council disapproval or modification by a two-thirds vote.

findings.plain: The City Map, the official registry of streets and publicly owned land, is still kept on paper across the five borough president offices.
findings.quote: The Map is over 8,000 individual paper maps administered by the offices of the five Borough Presidents.

recommendations: Vote yes on Question 2, creating fast track reviews for affordable housing through the Board of Standards and Appeals and for mixed-income residential projects in the neighborhoods that produce the least affordable housing.
Vote yes on Question 3, creating an Expedited Land Use Review Procedure for three types of zoning proposals.
Vote yes on Question 4, creating an Affordable Housing Appeals Board.
Vote yes on Question 5, modernizing administration of the City Map.
